chunks: And in the narration of Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:
There is no harm in salam for goods when you describe the length and width, and for animals when you describe their teeth.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the authority cited in the report
key_terms.أَسْنَانَهُ: the animal’s teeth, used to identify its age or stage
key_terms.السَّلَمِ: advance payment sale for a specified item to be delivered later
key_terms.الطُّولَ: the length measurement of the goods
key_terms.الْعَرْضَ: the width measurement of the goods
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurārah, the narrator reporting this hadith

ai.seo_question: When is salam (advance payment sale) permissible for goods and animals in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the permissibility of salam transactions in goods and animals when the item is described clearly enough to remove ambiguity. It emphasizes specification in commercial exchange, such as dimensions for goods and dental age markers for animals.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3953 - In a narration from Zurarah who reported from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
"There is no harm in Salam (advance payment) for goods if you describe their length and width, and for animals if you describe their age."
